evidence_cards.document_title: Scalability and performance in distributed graph databases
evidence_cards.main_contribution: This paper presents a comparative analysis of four graph partitioning strategies (Random Vertex, Metis-based, Random Edge, and HDRF) spanning both edge-cut and vertex-cut paradigms for distributed graph databases, evaluating them on metrics including edge cut, replication factor, load balance, latency, and throughput. It shows HDRF provides superior performance and scalability for dynamic, power-law networks.
